reasons: Missing-behaviour classification is well supported: Section 8.1 sets a three-year term and Section 9 (9.1–9.3, 9.5) contains only cause-based rights, so the absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation under T4C's detection guidance.

The inserted clause tracks the model language closely (30 days' written notice, pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, no early-termination fee) and adds the preferred-position confirmation that Vendor has no convenience right during a term, so the edit is directionally pro-Customer and rule-complete.

The Section 2.1 conforming edit is necessary, not overreach: a $2,000,000/year take-or-pay 'without ... termination rights' would otherwise nullify the new right and operate as a penalty; only 'or termination' is deleted and a narrow proviso tied to Section 9 is added, so the 0.667 changed-character ratio reflects the short source sentence rather than a non-minimal rewrite.
Comment complies with tone rules: correct [Playbook] prefix, first person plural, states what changed and why, cites the playbook position, and offers the 60-day fallback without lecturing.
Minor drafting nit (not disqualifying): the inserted clause is unnumbered even though the rationale calls it 'new 9.4' and Section 9 skips from 9.3 to 9.5 — add the '9.4' label for clean insertion.
